questions.prompt: For Zn(s)+Cu2+(aq)→Zn2+(aq)+Cu(s), Q=[Zn2+]/[Cu2+]. At fixed temperature, [Zn2+] is increased while [Cu2+] is unchanged. What happens to the cell potential for the written direction?
options: It increases because more product always strengthens the forward drive
E° changes by the same amount as Q
It is unchanged because zinc metal is omitted from Q
It decreases because Q increases.
questions.explanation: D is correct. In E=E°−(RT/nF)lnQ, the larger positive coefficient-times-log subtraction lowers E. A is incorrect: more dissolved product raises Q and reduces the written-direction driving force. B is incorrect: E° is unchanged at fixed temperature. C is incorrect: dissolved Zn2+ is included even though pure Zn is omitted.

questions.prompt: For the Zn/Cu reaction with Q=[Zn2+]/[Cu2+], [Cu2+] is increased at fixed [Zn2+] and temperature. Which potential trend follows?
options: E decreases because Q increases
E increases because Q decreases.
E° increases because a reactant was added
E must become exactly zero regardless of concentrations
questions.explanation: B is correct. A larger denominator lowers lnQ, making the subtracted term smaller. A is incorrect: the quotient denominator, not numerator, was increased. C is incorrect: standard potential remains fixed at the same temperature. D is incorrect: zero potential occurs at Q=K, not after any addition.

questions.prompt: The final ion concentration in a Zn half-cell is halved while the Cu2+ concentration and temperature are held fixed. What qualitative change follows for the Zn+Cu2+ reaction potential?
options: It decreases because every dilution reduces every cell voltage
It stays fixed because both ions have charge2+
It increases as the product/reactant quotient falls.
The standard potential necessarily changes sign
questions.explanation: C is correct. The Zn2+ numerator is halved, lowering Q and increasing E in the Nernst relationship. A is incorrect: the effect depends on which active species is changed. B is incorrect: equal charge does not cancel a concentration change in only one species. D is incorrect: composition changes do not alter E°.

questions.prompt: Under the concentration/activity model for a cell, what condition gives E=E° at the stated temperature?
options: Q=K for every possible cell
Equal masses of the two electrodes
questions.explanation: A is correct. The correction term vanishes because ln1=0. B is incorrect: ln0 is undefined and not the standard quotient condition. C is incorrect: that gives E=0, not generally E°. D is incorrect: pure-metal masses do not specify Q.

questions.prompt: What happens to a cell potential when the reacting system reaches equilibrium at Q=K?
options: E must equal E° even when K≠1
E becomes zero for the reaction.
E must increase without limit
The equilibrium constant becomes zero
questions.explanation: B is correct. At equilibrium there is no net thermodynamic driving force for that reaction. A is incorrect: standard composition and equilibrium are different conditions. C is incorrect: the driving force vanishes at equilibrium. D is incorrect: K remains a positive property of the reaction and temperature.

questions.prompt: For a written redox direction at fixed temperature, Q>K. Which potential sign is consistent with the direction needed to approach equilibrium?
options: E>0 for the written direction
E=0 because Q is finite
The sign cannot depend on concentrations
E<0 for the written direction; the reverse direction is favored.
questions.explanation: D is correct. Using E=(RT/nF)ln(K/Q), Q>K gives a negative logarithm. A is incorrect: that would favor moving farther in the wrong thermodynamic direction. B is incorrect: zero requires Q=K. C is incorrect: nonstandard concentrations determine Q and can affect the sign.

questions.prompt: A copper concentration cell has identical Cu electrodes in0.010 M and1.0 M Cu2+ solutions at the same temperature. Which operating direction reduces the concentration difference?
options: Cu dissolves in the dilute half-cell and Cu2+ plates in the concentrated half-cell.
Cu plates on the dilute side and dissolves on the concentrated side
Both electrodes dissolve without any reduction
No voltage is possible because the metals are identical
questions.explanation: A is correct. Oxidation raises dilute-side ion concentration while reduction lowers concentrated-side ion concentration; electrons travel through the wire from dilute-side metal to concentrated-side metal. B is incorrect: that would increase the concentration difference. C is incorrect: electron production requires a corresponding consumption process. D is incorrect: a concentration difference can supply a driving force.

questions.prompt: A concentration cell has identical electrodes and identical active-ion concentrations at the same temperature. No other gradient is present. What is its initial thermodynamic potential?
options: The potential of two different metals chosen from a table
Always one volt
Zero
Infinite because both ion concentrations match
questions.explanation: C is correct. With no concentration difference or other asymmetry, there is no net reaction driving force. A is incorrect: the electrodes are identical, so that difference is absent. B is incorrect: there is no universal one-volt value. D is incorrect: equal concentrations remove rather than maximize this driving force.

questions.prompt: During ideal discharge of a galvanic cell in its favorable direction, Q approaches K. What happens to the magnitude of its thermodynamic cell potential?
options: It approaches zero.
It increases without limit
It stays equal to E° for every composition
It must reverse sign before equilibrium is reached
questions.explanation: A is correct. As the reacting composition approaches equilibrium, the driving force for further discharge diminishes. B is incorrect: equilibrium is the zero-driving-force condition. C is incorrect: the nonstandard correction changes with Q. D is incorrect: the favorable-direction potential can decrease to zero without first reversing.

questions.prompt: A cell reaction has positive E° but is placed in a nonstandard composition with Q>K. Which claim is correct?
options: Its potential must remain positive because E° is positive
Its potential for the written direction can be negative despite positive E°.
Its standard potential has permanently become negative
The setup disproves the equilibrium constant relationship
questions.explanation: B is correct. Standard favorability does not guarantee forward favorability at every possible composition. A is incorrect: the concentration correction can outweigh E°. C is incorrect: E° is not changed by the chosen concentrations. D is incorrect: the relationship predicts this possible reversal.

questions.prompt: For Zn+Cu2+→Zn2++Cu, both active-ion concentrations are multiplied by the same factor at constant temperature, with ideal behavior. What happens to E?
options: It doubles whenever both concentrations double
It must become zero because the scaling factors match
E° changes by the concentration factor
It stays the same because [Zn2+]/[Cu2+] is unchanged.
questions.explanation: D is correct. Only their ratio enters Q for this reaction; equal scaling cancels. A is incorrect: potential does not scale with the concentration sum. B is incorrect: an unchanged ratio need not equal K. C is incorrect: standard potential is fixed at the temperature.
